context:
Goal: every part of every ruling lands as a step, and nothing is silently partial.
Problem (rule): a ruling's parts reach the roadmap only through triage's reading of the plan, and no check compares them; the one-store part of your R28 ruling (page data in one store) dropped.
Based on (measured): 47 plan rulings each have at least one step, yet R28's one-store part had none until step page-data-one-store today (record branch commit 87d1e99b0).
Based on (read): the feedback log's check proves only that a step file exists for an item.
Departs from: a plan ruling on main cites no step ids — each numbered part names its step id, a check compares them, and the re-rank agent reads the plan against the roadmap.
Meanwhile: nothing waits on this; pick either or both.

lastAnswer.note: Owner picked both in chat, 11:31 CST Nov 12, relayed by the retrospective 11:32 CST: "probably both is fine -- and note that the id's probably need good tagging right slugs or whatever or that won't matter here?" Filed as step ruling-parts-cite-steps (plan cites step:<slug>; an opaque id such as c55 carries a short gloss).

options.gain: A dropped part shows at once, by a check, not by memory.
options.how: Each numbered part of a plan ruling names its step id. A check on the plan, at each push, flags a part with no step or a step that no longer exists; triage files the missing.
options.label: Step id per part, checked
options.lose: One id per part to write; a small check to build.

options.gain: No new check; it rides a step already queued.
options.how: At each batch merge the agent from step queue-score-plus-agent (your pick d at 11:24 CST) reads the plan's rulings against the steps and files what is missing.
options.label: The re-rank agent reads plan against roadmap
options.lose: A model's reading, so a part can still slip.

ref: step page-data-one-store; step queue-score-plus-agent; ruling R28
reply: Tracked as roadmap step ruling-parts-cite-steps, home decision session-tiers.
title: How should every part of a ruling be sure to land as a roadmap step?
why: Recommended: both. a catches a drop by check; b catches what a check cannot read, such as a part worded loosely.
